extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys and agents), USPTO disciplinary stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order describing practitioner duties under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, the legal conclusions for violations, and the sanctions/administrative requirements (suspension, probation, compliance, reinstatement) applicable to a registered patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 — Competent representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall provide competent representation (37 C.F.R. § 11.101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of failing competent representation cited: not informing client of a Notice to File Missing Parts and not responding (leading to abandonment of the application); failing to file claims in an international application and failing to respond to an Invitation to Correct (resulting in no international filing date). The Order ties these failures to lack of competence in performing patent prosecution services (drafting, filing, prosecuting).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.102(a) — Abide by client's decisions / consult on means
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall abide by a client's decisions concerning the objectives of the representation and consult with the client as to the means by which those objectives are to be pursued (37 C.F.R. § 11.102(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited failures: failing to revive a client-desired abandoned application and failing to submit annuity fees the client believed would be timely paid. Emphasis on practitioner consulting and following client's objectives when deciding procedural steps (e.g., revival vs. alternative filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — Diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client (37 C.F.R. § 11.103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: allowing an application to go abandoned by not responding to an Office notice; failing to timely respond to an Invitation to Correct (losing an international filing date); failing to timely file renewal/annuity payments (causing late fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(1) — Promptly inform client when informed consent required
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall promptly inform the client of any circumstance to which the client's informed consent is required by the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited misconduct: not adequately communicating material information or clearly explaining the material risks of, and reasonably available alternatives to, applying new payments to outstanding balances; taking earmarked payments (e.g., $5,000 for a new application) and applying them to past invoices without ensuring client consent; accepting annuity payments without obtaining informed consent to apply them to outstanding balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2) — Reasonable consultation about means
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall reasonably consult with the client about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited failures: not informing client of a Notice to File Missing Parts and consequences of not reviving the application; not informing client about the failure to include claims leading to an Invitation to Correct and implications for international filing; not consulting/ notifying client that payments earmarked for foreign annuities would instead be applied to outstanding balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3) — Keep client reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the Order: failing to inform client of Notice to File Missing Parts, Notice of Abandonment, Invitation to Correct, and Notification of Non-treatment as an international application; failing to forward USPTO correspondence after termination of the attorney-client relationship; failing to inform client of deadlines for annuity payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.105(b) — Communicate scope of representation and basis/rate of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall communicate to the client the scope of the representation and the basis or the rate of the fee and expenses for which the client will be responsible (37 C.F.R. § 11.105(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited misconduct: failing to clearly communicate that new payments would be applied to outstanding balances first; failing to explain how a $5,000 payment earmarked for a new application would instead be applied to prior invoices; failing to explain the basis/rate and application of annuity fees prior to applying them to outstanding balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.107(a)(2) and (b) — Conflicts of interest / informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not represent a client if the representation involves a significant risk that the representation will be materially limited by the personal interest of the practitioner, absent informed consent confirmed in writing (37 C.F.R. § 11.107(a)(2) and (b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to the facts: practitioner had a competing personal interest in applying new client payments to outstanding balances, but failed to adequately disclose the conflict and obtain informed written consent; failing to explain material risks and alternatives created a significant risk of material limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.116(d) — Duties upon termination of representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon termination of representation, a practitioner shall take steps to the extent reasonably practicable to protect a client's interests, e.g., give reasonable notice, allow time for employment of other counsel, surrender papers and property to which the client is entitled, and refund any advance payment of fee or expense that has not been earned or incurred (37 C.F.R. § 11.116(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited failures: after termination, not forwarding a Receiving Office notice that an international application would not be treated as such; not forwarding USPTO correspondence about another application (withdrawal not accepted, non-final rejection, notice of new correspondence); not returning or properly accounting for client funds intended for annuities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions / Conditions of Probation (agreed-upon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions ordered: 30-day suspension (commencing 14 days after the Final Order), followed by a 12-month probationary period during which specified conditions must be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (1) take the Multistate Professional Responsibility Exam (MPRE) and attain a score of 86 or higher; (2) take at least three (3.0) hours of continuing legal education credit concerning law firm management and client trust accounts; (3) provide sworn affidavit and documentary evidence of compliance prior to or during the probationary period. Failure to comply may trigger an Order to Show Cause and possible additional suspension of up to 11 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 — Duties and restrictions during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: During suspension practitioner must: provide notice of suspension to State and Federal jurisdictions to which admitted; notify clients with immediate or prospective business before the Office and arrange for legal services; notify opposing practitioners/parties in Office matters; not hold oneself out as authorized to practice before the Office; not render legal advice or services for matters before the Office (37 C.F.R. § 11.58).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order lists five specific duties (notice to jurisdictions, notice to clients and arrangements for services, notice to opposing counsel/parties, prohibition on holding out authorization to practice, prohibition on rendering legal advice for Office matters). The Order also specifies certain duties that the respondent will not have unless reinstatement is not granted within 90 days (e.g., not required to file notice of withdrawal in each pending application, not required to deliver documents to all clients, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of compliance under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must provide an affidavit of compliance certifying compliance with the Agreement and 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(d), appended with specified evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appended to the affidavit must be: (1) a copy of each form of notice sent, names and addresses of recipients, and all return receipts or returned mail; and (2) a list of all other State, Federal, and administrative jurisdictions to which the practitioner is admitted. The order also specifies materials the affidavit need not append (e.g., bank account schedules, schedules describing disposition of client funds, proof of distribution/closing of accounts, or affidavits describing removal of advertisements), as set forth in § 11.58(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 — Petition for reinstatement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may not resume practice before the Office until reinstated by order; after suspension and compliance with § 11.58, respondent may file a petition for reinstatement that must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(b)-(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include filing the petition with required fee, attesting to compliance (including sworn declaration that practitioner has not practiced before the Office during suspension), complying with provisions of § 11.60(c)(1)-(3). The OED may elect not to publish notice of the petition as set forth in § 11.60(h)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication & administrative posting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides the text and content elements to be included in the Official Gazette notice (identifying violations, sanctions, and summary facts). It also states the Final Order will be electronically published on the OED FOIA Reading Room accessible at the specified URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future use of disciplinary record
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in future matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be considered: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning respondent; (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against respondent as an aggravating factor in determining discipline or to rebut statements by respondent. This is an explicit warning that this record may be relied upon later.
